turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: Atlas Auto Group exec sponsor Mon, Oct 12, 2026, 3:00PM • 7:59

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 0:05 Hey [PERSON_2], hey [PERSON_3]. Uh, Thanks for hopping on. How's Phoenix treating you? Still triple digits?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 0:11 Oh man, it finally broke. We hit 94 yesterday. Practically sweater weather.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 0:15 Sweater weather. Sure. My AC disagrees.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_4] 0:19 [PERSON_3], uh, good to see you again. [PERSON_2], I caught the tail end of the Cardinals game. That fourth quarter was rough.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 0:29 Don't. I was there. My son kept asking why we stayed. I didn't have a good answer.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 0:36 Ha. Well, we appreciate you both making time. I know it's a busy week.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 0:43 It It is. So let me just jump in. We're about seven weeks out from the renewal and I've got to put a number in front of the budget committee.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 0:55 And we've got some other folks sniffing around, so we figured it was time to talk.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_4] 1:02 Yeah, we heard that. That's part of why I asked to join. What are you hearing?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 1:09 I'll be straight with you, I've been asked to bring two options to the December budget meeting, and you're one of them.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:18 Okay. That's fair. Can I ask what the other option looks like?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 1:23 Marchex is offering a flat rate per rooftop that's about thirty percent under what we pay you, and they'll include the call scoring.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_4] 1:33 Per rooftop, flat. So no seat math, no usage tiers?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 1:38 Flat. Twenty-two rooftops, one number. That's the pitch. And it's clean, I'll give them that. My job is easier with a flat line item.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 1:48 It's not just um, the price though. I mean, price matters, um, obviously. But the thing that's been bugging my team is the Google side.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 1:58 The offline conversions?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 2:01 Yeah. The conversions are landing in Google Ads late. Like two days late. My paid search manager shows me reports and the numbers don't match what we see in Invoca until Wednesday. By then we've already made bid decisions on bad data.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_4] 2:16 How long has that been going on?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 2:20 A A few weeks? Maybe a month. It wasn't always like that.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 2:26 And to be clear, that's not a billing thing. That's a, what do you call it, um, a confidence thing. If the data's late, I mean, I can't defend the spend.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 2:37 Got it. Uh, Let me write that down. Two days late, started roughly a month ago. Is it it every conversion or some?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 2:46 I'd have to check. Like, my gut says most of them. The GCLID matching seems fine, it's just... late.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 2:54 Okay. I don't want to guess at a cause on this call. Let me pull the integration logs and get our support team looking at the timing, and I'll come back to you with what we find.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 3:11 How long does that take?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 3:14 I'll have an update for you by Thursday.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 3:17 Thursday's fine. But I need to know if this is a fix or a, you know, a known thing we live with.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_4] 3:27 We'll be honest with you either way.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 3:30 The Google conversions being two days late is the thing that makes Marchex sound good. Fix that and half this conversation goes away.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 3:41 Half. He said half, I heard half.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 3:44 I'm being generous. The other half is still the thirty percent.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_4] 3:49 Understood. And I'm not going to sit here and tell you we'll beat a flat per-rooftop rate line for line. What I can tell you is what you'd be giving up, and then you decide.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 4:05 That's the thing. I need it in numbers, not a story. What does Invoca actually save us or make us?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_4] 4:14 So the call tracking and attribution side, that's the core. Every call from your Google and Meta campaigns gets attributed back to the campaign, the keyword, the page. That's what feeds your bidding. If that goes away or gets worse, your cost per lead drifts.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 4:32 Drifts how much?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_4] 4:34 I don't have a number I can stand behind for you today. I can have [PERSON_1] pull your call volume and conversion mix and we can model it.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 4:47 Model it. Okay. I like models.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 4:51 He really does. He has a spreadsheet for his fantasy league.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 4:57 It's a good spreadsheet.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 4:59 I'd like to see that. Okay, so, what I'm hearing is two things. One, the Google timing issue. So, Two, the flat rate comparison. Anything else on the table?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 5:11 The Salesforce side is fine. Leads are writing over, the BDC sees them, nobody's complaining.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 5:17 Yeah, that's been solid.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 5:20 Good. And the signal side? Your appointment booked and quote given signals?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 5:25 Those are working. That's actually why the the scoring thing in the Marchex pitch caught my eye, but it sounds like it's in the same bucket.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 5:36 Right. So the question I have to answer is, do we pay thirty percent less for roughly the same thing, or do we pay you and get whatever it is we're getting that's worth thirty percent?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_4] 5:50 That's the right question. And I'd um, rather answer it with your data than with a slide.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 5:57 When can you get me something? Because I present on the eighth of December.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_4] 6:04 Give us two weeks. [PERSON_1] and I will build a side-by-side, your current cost, what the switch would you know, actually cost you all-in, and what changes operationally.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 6:17 And I'll fold in the Google timing update by Thursday so that's not hanging over the whole thing.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 6:25 Good. And [PERSON_4], I'll say this plainly. I'm not trying to squeeze you. I have a mandate to cut vendor spend where it makes sense. If it doesn't make sense, I'll say so.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_4] 6:39 That's all I can ask. I'd rather you uh, tell me no with a reason than yes with a grudge.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 6:46 He's a grudge guy. You don't want that.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 6:49 I heard that.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 6:51 You were supposed to.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 6:54 Okay, so action items. I'll dig into the Google conversion timing and come back Thursday. [PERSON_4] and I will pull together the comparison and get it to to you by, let's say the twenty-sixth?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 7:06 Twenty-sixth works. That gives me a week before I um, have to lock the deck.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_4] 7:13 And [PERSON_3], so, one more thing. If there's a specific rooftop or two where the pain is worst, tell [PERSON_1]. It helps us focus.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 7:22 I'd say the Nevada stores. They've got the highest call volume and the thinnest margin, so late data hurts more there.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 7:31 Vegas and Henderson, yeah. Those two.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 7:34 Perfect. I'll note that.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 7:36 And hey, next time you're in Phoenix, we owe you a game. Assuming they can win one.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_4] 7:44 I'll take that bet. Thanks for the time, both of you.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_3] 7:49 Thanks [PERSON_4], [PERSON_1]. Thursday, you know, right?

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_1] 7:53 Thursday. Talk soon.

turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: [PERSON_2] 7:55 Take care, guys.
